chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Dawud ibn Sarhan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

It is not appropriate for a woman to leave herself without ornament, even if she just hangs a necklace on her neck. And it is not appropriate for her to leave her hand without dyeing, even if she just wipes it once with henna, even if she has aged.

key_terms.الحناء: Henna: a natural plant-based dye used for decorating hands and hair
key_terms.الخضاب: Khidab: dyeing (especially hands/hair with henna); a form of beautification
key_terms.تعطل: To leave without ornament or adornment (ta'til); to neglect beautification
key_terms.قلادة: Qiladah: necklace; a basic form of women's jewelry

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about women's adornment and wearing jewelry in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advised that women should always maintain some form of self-adornment and personal beautification. Even a simple necklace or a light application of henna suffices, and this applies even to elderly women. This teaching was delivered in the context of daily life guidance, emphasizing that self-care and beautification are not vanities but recommended practices in Islam, often understood as a wife's care for her appearance for her husband's sake.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti from Dawud b. Sarhan. He said: Abu `Abdillah (as) said:

It is not appropriate for a woman to be without ornament, even if she just hangs a necklace on her neck. It is not appropriate for her to leave off dyeing her hand, even if she just wipes it once with henna, even if she has aged.
